key_findings: **The named 'binders' are actually OWNER CLASS CTORS** (LuaDebugLog::ctor + LuaDebugSelect::ctor), not separate binder methods. The 'binder' framing was a misread - the owner ctor itself constructs all handler objects + subscribes them inline. Single-binder-per-owner-class from the is technically true (each owner has one ctor) but it's better framed as ctor-integrated subscription rather than a separate binder pattern.

**The HEAP FACTORY PATTERN generalizes from Receivers to Elements**. Previously known for Receiver classes (BCS-Y-1023 SendLogReceiver, BCS-Y-1144 AchievementIdReceiver, BCS-Y-1145 VehicleGradeReceiver). The same shape holds for Element classes (BCS-Y-1330 LuaDebugLog, BCS-Y-1332 LuaDebugSelect). 117-byte body, simple alloc-and-ctor pattern, zero direct instruction-level callers. Suggests this is a GENERAL architectural pattern across all Sqwt heap-allocated classes - both UI Elements and Receivers.

**Inheritance chain RaptureElement <- XamlElement <- LuaDebugLog/Select**. XamlElement::ctor (BCS-Y-1334 FUN_00539890) chains to RaptureElement::ctor (BCS-Y-0539). XamlElement is the parent of both LuaDebug* classes AND likely of FormElement / CameraElement / TargetElement / Esrb / etc. - the 52 parent classes from the broader sweep are mostly under this XamlElement umbrella. Confirms a hierarchical Sqwt UI class tree with RaptureElement at the root.

**Subscription mechanism is target->vtable[+0xB4]->slot[+0x28](event_id, handler)**. The +0xB4 field offset and +0x28 slot offset (decimal 10) are STRUCTURAL CONSTANTS of the Sqwt event-source class layout. Every event source class has a secondary interface vtable embedded at +0xB4; that interface's slot[10] is the subscribe method. This is the Sqwt analog of WPF's INotifyPropertyChanged / event-handler pattern - a structural contract baked into class layout.

**Multi-handler-per-channel registration is supported**. LuaDebugLog::ctor registers TWO distinct KeyEventHandlers both subscribed to event channel DAT_01359614 but with different callback methods (FUN_00599880 and LAB_00599800). Event source supports broadcast to multiple subscribers - canonical multicast event pattern.

**LuaDebugSelect demonstrates the embedded-EventHandler optimization** (originally observed earlier). RoutedEventHandler is INLINE-CONSTRUCTED at +0xD0 (no heap alloc); SelectionChangedEventHandler is heap-allocated at +0xC8. Both subscribe via the same +0xB4/+0x28 mechanism. The choice between inline and heap likely reflects 1:1-with-owner-lifetime (inline) vs N:1 or dynamic (heap).
